paragraphs: Children in care across East Sussex, from Hastings and Bexhill to Eastbourne, Lewes and the Wealden villages, are looked after by East Sussex County Council's own fostering service and by the independent agencies and charities listed on this page. The council is responsible for finding a foster home for every child in its care, from newborn babies to teenagers, and says it looks first to its own carers. In February 2024 councillors were urged to help recruit more carers for the council's in-house service.

The council offers several kinds of fostering: short-term, long-term, emergency care, short breaks and a fostering 16+ scheme for older teenagers. Its April 2026 guidance says carers need to be over 21 and have a spare bedroom; no qualifications are needed because full training is provided. You can foster if you are single, retired, LGBTQ+, a renter, working or not working, not a parent yourself, a pet owner, or managing a disability or medical condition, and you can say which age range suits you.

Council carers receive a weekly maintenance allowance and a professional fostering fee, a locally based supervising social worker and a 24-hour helpline seven days a week. The council runs regular online information sessions at lunchtime and in the evening, including on 19 November and 16 December, and visits towns around the county with current carers. As agencies set their own fees and support, it is worth speaking to the council and two or three of the agencies below and comparing what each offers.
